:::: {.content-visible when-profile="deutsch"}
**Installation:** gehört zu CTM Assessment, siehe [Überblick und Installation](exp_extensions.qmd)
**Quelle:** [@jsxgraph], [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

Die Fassung von JSXGraph in CTM Assessment beruht auf der Extension `jsxgraph-quarto` und ergänzt eine **Bewertungsbrücke**: Eine Grafik kann damit die Antwort auf eine `math-exercise`-Aufgabe liefern. Die JSXGraph-Bibliothek wird beim Lesen aus dem Netz geladen, ihre Version legt das Paket fest.

```{.yaml filename="seite.qmd"}
engine: markdown      # nur nötig, wenn die Seite auch math-exercise enthält (Quarto 1.10+)
filters:
  - ctm-assessment
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## JSXGraph nicht noch einmal installieren
JSXGraph kommt mit `ctm-assessment` und liegt in `_extensions/jsxgraph/`. Ein zusätzliches `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto` landet verschachtelt in `_extensions/jsxgraph/jsxgraph/` und wird ignoriert. Beim Bauen erscheint dazu eine Warnung. Steht ein Einzelfilter wie `jsxgraph` im Kopf, ersetzt ihn `ctm-assessment`: Eine Seite führt entweder `ctm-assessment` auf oder einzelne Komponenten, nicht beides.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Beispiel

```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```

Zieh den Punkt $x$ auf der Achse.

## Schreibweise

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Schreib immer wörtlich `BOARDID`. Die Extension ersetzt es durch eine eindeutige Kennung.
Eine fest eingetragene Kennung macht Seiten mit mehreren Grafiken kaputt.
:::

Optionen stehen als Attribute am Block, z. B. Breite und Höhe:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph width="600" height="300"}
...
```
````

## Häufige Elemente

```{.javascript}
// Funktionsgraph
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd' });

// Verschiebbarer Punkt
var p = board.create('point', [2, 1], { name: 'P', size: 4 });

// Gleiter: Punkt, der an eine Linie oder Kurve gebunden ist
var g = board.create('glider', [1, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], { name: 'x' });

// Schieberegler
var s = board.create('slider', [[0,-3],[4,-3],[0,1,2*Math.PI]], { name: 'a' });

// Wert des Schiebereglers benutzen
board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return Math.sin(s.Value()*x); }]);

// Beschriftung
board.create('text', [1, 2, function() { return 'x = ' + g.X().toFixed(2); }]);

// Strecke
board.create('segment', [p1, p2], { strokeColor: '#198754', dash: 2 });
```

## Grafik als Antwort

Mit `assessment_id` und `JXG.QuartoAssessment.register(...)` meldet eine Grafik ihren Zustand an eine Aufgabe. Die Aufgabe holt ihn mit `response: jsxgraph:<assessment_id>` und prüft ihn mit eigenem Prüfcode:

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| label: exp-point-above
#| caption: Punkt über der Geraden
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Zieh den Punkt $P$ in den Bereich oberhalb der Geraden $y = x$.
```

Der Quelltext dazu:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Zieh den Punkt $P$ in den Bereich oberhalb der Geraden $y = x$.
```
````

`response` darf beliebige Daten zurückgeben, die sich als JSON schreiben lassen. `embed-response: true` setzt die Grafik in die Aufgabenkarte. Für Aufgaben, in denen Studierende einen Graphen aus Knoten und Kanten bauen, gibt es den fertigen Editor `JXG.QuartoGraphEditor`.

:::
::::

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="english"}
**Install:** part of CTM Assessment, see [Overview and installation](exp_extensions.qmd)
**Source:** [@jsxgraph], [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

The version of JSXGraph in CTM Assessment is based on the `jsxgraph-quarto` extension and adds an **assessment bridge**: a graph can supply the answer to a `math-exercise` exercise. The JSXGraph library is loaded from the network at read time; the package fixes its version.

```{.yaml filename="page.qmd"}
engine: markdown      # only needed if the page also contains math-exercise (Quarto 1.10+)
filters:
  - ctm-assessment
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not install JSXGraph a second time
JSXGraph comes with `ctm-assessment` and sits in `_extensions/jsxgraph/`. An additional `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto` ends up nested in `_extensions/jsxgraph/jsxgraph/` and is ignored. The build prints a warning about it. If a single filter such as `jsxgraph` is listed in the header, `ctm-assessment` replaces it: a page lists either `ctm-assessment` or individual components, not both.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Example

```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```

Drag the point $x$ along the axis.

## Syntax

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Always use the literal string `BOARDID`. The extension replaces it with a unique ID.
Hardcoding an ID breaks pages with several graphs.
:::

Options are written as attributes on the block, e.g. width and height:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph width="600" height="300"}
...
```
````

## Common elements

```{.javascript}
// Function graph
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd' });

// Draggable point
var p = board.create('point', [2, 1], { name: 'P', size: 4 });

// Glider: point constrained to a line or curve
var g = board.create('glider', [1, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], { name: 'x' });

// Slider
var s = board.create('slider', [[0,-3],[4,-3],[0,1,2*Math.PI]], { name: 'a' });

// Use slider value
board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return Math.sin(s.Value()*x); }]);

// Text label
board.create('text', [1, 2, function() { return 'x = ' + g.X().toFixed(2); }]);

// Segment
board.create('segment', [p1, p2], { strokeColor: '#198754', dash: 2 });
```

## Graph as answer

With `assessment_id` and `JXG.QuartoAssessment.register(...)`, a graph reports its state to an exercise. The exercise fetches it with `response: jsxgraph:<assessment_id>` and checks it with its own checking code:

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board-en"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| label: exp-point-above-en
#| caption: Point above the line
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board-en
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Drag the point $P$ into the region above the line $y = x$.
```

The source for it:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Drag the point $P$ into the region above the line $y = x$.
```
````

`response` may return any data that can be written as JSON. `embed-response: true` moves the graph into the exercise card. For exercises in which students build a graph of vertices and edges, there is the ready-made editor `JXG.QuartoGraphEditor`.

:::
::::

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="svenska"}
**Installation:** ingår i CTM Assessment, se [Översikt och installation](exp_extensions.qmd)
**Källa:** [@jsxgraph], [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

JSXGraph-versionen i CTM Assessment bygger på tillägget `jsxgraph-quarto` och lägger till en **bedömningsbrygga**: en graf kan leverera svaret på en `math-exercise`-uppgift. JSXGraph-biblioteket laddas från nätet när sidan läses, och paketet bestämmer vilken version som används.

```{.yaml filename="sida.qmd"}
engine: markdown      # behövs bara om sidan också innehåller math-exercise (Quarto 1.10+)
filters:
  - ctm-assessment
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Installera inte JSXGraph en gång till
JSXGraph följer med `ctm-assessment` och ligger i `_extensions/jsxgraph/`. Ett extra `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto` hamnar nästlat i `_extensions/jsxgraph/jsxgraph/` och ignoreras. Bygget skriver ut en varning om det. Står ett enskilt filter som `jsxgraph` i sidhuvudet ersätter `ctm-assessment` det: en sida anger antingen `ctm-assessment` eller enskilda komponenter, inte båda.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Exempel

```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```

Dra punkten $x$ längs axeln.

## Syntax

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Använd alltid den bokstavliga strängen `BOARDID`. Tillägget ersätter den med ett unikt id.
Ett fast id förstör sidor med flera grafer.
:::

Inställningar skrivs som attribut på blocket, t.ex. bredd och höjd:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph width="600" height="300"}
...
```
````

## Vanliga element

```{.javascript}
// Function graph
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd' });

// Draggable point
var p = board.create('point', [2, 1], { name: 'P', size: 4 });

// Glider: point constrained to a line or curve
var g = board.create('glider', [1, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], { name: 'x' });

// Slider
var s = board.create('slider', [[0,-3],[4,-3],[0,1,2*Math.PI]], { name: 'a' });

// Use slider value
board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return Math.sin(s.Value()*x); }]);

// Text label
board.create('text', [1, 2, function() { return 'x = ' + g.X().toFixed(2); }]);

// Segment
board.create('segment', [p1, p2], { strokeColor: '#198754', dash: 2 });
```

## Graf som svar

Med `assessment_id` och `JXG.QuartoAssessment.register(...)` rapporterar en graf sitt tillstånd till en uppgift. Uppgiften hämtar det med `response: jsxgraph:<assessment_id>` och kontrollerar det med sin egen kontrollkod:

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board-sv"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| label: exp-point-above-sv
#| caption: Punkt ovanför linjen
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board-sv
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Dra punkten $P$ till området ovanför linjen $y = x$.
```

Källkoden till det:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Drag the point $P$ into the region above the line $y = x$.
```
````

`response` får returnera vilka data som helst som kan skrivas som JSON. `embed-response: true` flyttar in grafen i uppgiftens ruta. För uppgifter där studenterna bygger en graf av noder och kanter finns den färdiga redigeraren `JXG.QuartoGraphEditor`.

:::

:::: {.content-visible when-profile="norsk"}
**Installasjon:** er en del av CTM Assessment, se [Oversikt og installasjon](exp_extensions.qmd)
**Kilde:** [@jsxgraph], [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

JSXGraph-versjonen i CTM Assessment bygger på utvidelsen `jsxgraph-quarto` og legger til en **vurderingsbro**: en graf kan levere svaret på en `math-exercise`-oppgave. JSXGraph-biblioteket lastes fra nettet når siden leses, og pakken bestemmer hvilken versjon som brukes.

```{.yaml filename="side.qmd"}
engine: markdown      # trengs bare hvis siden også inneholder math-exercise (Quarto 1.10+)
filters:
  - ctm-assessment
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Ikke installer JSXGraph en gang til
JSXGraph følger med `ctm-assessment` og ligger i `_extensions/jsxgraph/`. Et ekstra `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto` havner nestet i `_extensions/jsxgraph/jsxgraph/` og blir ignorert. Byggingen skriver ut en advarsel om det. Står et enkeltfilter som `jsxgraph` i sidehodet, erstatter `ctm-assessment` det: en side oppgir enten `ctm-assessment` eller enkeltkomponenter, ikke begge.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Eksempel

```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```

Dra punktet $x$ langs aksen.

## Syntaks

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Bruk alltid den bokstavelige strengen `BOARDID`. Utvidelsen erstatter den med en unik ID.
En fast ID ødelegger sider med flere grafer.
:::

Innstillinger skrives som attributter på blokken, f.eks. bredde og høyde:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph width="600" height="300"}
...
```
````

## Graf som svar

Med `assessment_id` og `JXG.QuartoAssessment.register(...)` melder en graf tilstanden sin til en oppgave. Oppgaven henter den med `response: jsxgraph:<assessment_id>` og kontrollerer den med sin egen kontrollkode:

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board-no"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});

```


Kildekoden til dette:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({

```

Drag the point $P$ into the region above the line $y = x$.
```
````

`response` kan returnere alle data som kan skrives som JSON. `embed-response: true` flytter grafen inn i oppgaveboksen. Til oppgaver der studentene bygger en graf av noder og kanter, finnes den ferdige editoren `JXG.QuartoGraphEditor`.

**Installation:** er en del af CTM Assessment, se [Oversigt og installation](exp_extensions.qmd)
**Kilde:** [@jsxgraph], [github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto](https://github.com/jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto)

JSXGraph-versionen i CTM Assessment bygger på udvidelsen `jsxgraph-quarto` og tilføjer en **bedømmelsesbro**: en graf kan levere svaret på en `math-exercise`-opgave. JSXGraph-biblioteket hentes fra nettet, når siden læses, og pakken bestemmer, hvilken version der bruges.

```{.yaml filename="side.qmd"}
engine: markdown      # kun nødvendigt, hvis siden også indeholder math-exercise (Quarto 1.10+)
filters:
  - ctm-assessment
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Installér ikke JSXGraph en gang til
JSXGraph følger med `ctm-assessment` og ligger i `_extensions/jsxgraph/`. Et ekstra `quarto add jsxgraph/jsxgraph-quarto` havner indlejret i `_extensions/jsxgraph/jsxgraph/` og bliver ignoreret. Bygningen udskriver en advarsel om det. Står et enkeltfilter som `jsxgraph` i sidehovedet, erstatter `ctm-assessment` det: en side angiver enten `ctm-assessment` eller enkelte komponenter, ikke begge.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Eksempel

```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-7, 1.8, 7, -1.8],
    axis: true,
    showNavigation: false
});
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], {
    strokeColor: '#0d6efd', strokeWidth: 2.5
});
var p = board.create('glider', [1.57, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], {
    name: 'x', size: 5, fillColor: '#E91E63'
});
board.create('point', [
    function() { return p.X(); },
    function() { return Math.sin(p.X()); }
], { name: function() { return 'sin(x) ≈ ' + Math.sin(p.X()).toFixed(3); },
     size: 5, fillColor: '#198754', fixed: true });
```

Træk punktet $x$ langs aksen.

## Syntaks

````{.markdown}
```jsxgraph
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5],   // [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]
    axis: true,
    keepaspectratio: false,
    showNavigation: false
});
```
````

::: {.callout-important}
Brug altid den bogstavelige streng `BOARDID`. Udvidelsen erstatter den med et entydigt id.
Et fast id ødelægger sider med flere grafer.
:::

Indstillinger skrives som attributter på blokken, f.eks. bredde og højde:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph width="600" height="300"}
...
```
````

## Almindelige elementer

```{.javascript}
// Function graph
board.create('functiongraph', [Math.sin], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd' });

// Draggable point
var p = board.create('point', [2, 1], { name: 'P', size: 4 });

// Glider: point constrained to a line or curve
var g = board.create('glider', [1, 0, board.defaultAxes.x], { name: 'x' });

// Slider
var s = board.create('slider', [[0,-3],[4,-3],[0,1,2*Math.PI]], { name: 'a' });

// Use slider value
board.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return Math.sin(s.Value()*x); }]);

// Text label
board.create('text', [1, 2, function() { return 'x = ' + g.X().toFixed(2); }]);

// Segment
board.create('segment', [p1, p2], { strokeColor: '#198754', dash: 2 });
```

## Graf som svar

Med `assessment_id` og `JXG.QuartoAssessment.register(...)` melder en graf sin tilstand til en opgave. Opgaven henter den med `response: jsxgraph:<assessment_id>` og kontrollerer den med sin egen kontrolkode:

```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board-da"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| label: exp-point-above-da
#| caption: Punkt over linjen
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board-da
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Træk punktet $P$ ind i området over linjen $y = x$.
```

Kildekoden til det:

````{.markdown}
```{.jsxgraph assessment_id="exp-board"}
var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(BOARDID, {
    boundingbox: [-5, 5, 5, -5], axis: true, showNavigation: false
});
board.create('line', [[0, 0], [1, 1]], { strokeColor: '#0d6efd', fixed: true });
var point = board.create('point', [2, -1], { name: 'P', size: 5 });

JXG.QuartoAssessment.register({
  board: board,
  response: function () {
    return { point: [point.X(), point.Y()] };
  }
});
```

```{math-exercise}
#| mode: custom
#| response: jsxgraph:exp-board
#| embed-response: true
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       x, y = response["point"]
#|       return {"score": 1 if y > x else 0}

Drag the point $P$ into the region above the line $y = x$.
```
````

`response` må returnere alle data, der kan skrives som JSON. `embed-response: true` flytter grafen ind i opgaveboksen. Til opgaver, hvor de studerende bygger en graf af knuder og kanter, findes den færdige editor `JXG.QuartoGraphEditor`.

:::
